position: Delete the UI column. Do not install tokens-hook.sh as written. The existence of unused plumbing is sunk cost, not a mandate — and wiring it today would ship a number that is not cost, not context, not throughput, may systematically under-count the fleet's actual workload (C5), and deliberately corrupts the requests metric (C1) to get there. aigate already has a working usage-limit/reset signal via the account poller; nobody in this brief has named a decision the composite tokens sum enables that that signal does not. Revisit only after the U2 experiment falsifies under-count and someone defines what the column is actually for.

claims.claim: Server accepts, aggregates, and renders tokens; the only missing link is a producer that is never invoked
claims.evidence: Brief F1/F2: src/server.js schema/insert/aggregate; clients/tokens-hook.sh present; grep tokens-hook clients/install.sh empty; Stop hooks in settings.json are aaa-selfimprove.sh and nohumans.js only

claims.claim: Production tokens column has never carried real telemetry
claims.evidence: Brief F3: GET /api/stats on prod — 11,167 requests, 13 tokens total

claims.claim: Installing tokens-hook.sh as written roughly doubles displayed request counts
claims.evidence: Hook header / brief C1: no UPDATE endpoint; Stop posts a second request_log row with prompt:""; aggregate sums requests as row count

claims.claim: The summed token figure (in+out+cache_write+cache_read) is not cost, context size, or billed usage
claims.evidence: Anthropic bills cache-read at a discount vs input; hook sums raw counts into one integer; column header is undifferentiated 'tokens'

claims.claim: Last-assistant-message-only read under-counts multi-step tool-use turns
claims.evidence: Brief C5/U1/U2 — no transcript fixture or live capture in evidence bundle; depends entirely on whether usage blocks are per-message or cumulative
claims.test: Run experiment E1 below on a multi-tool turn

claims.claim: tokens column is redundant with the account poller's limit/reset path for aigate's core job (usage-aware account selection)
claims.evidence: Brief product context: selector already tracks per-account usage limits and reset windows by another path; tokens column empty in prod with no reported decision failure attributed to it
claims.test: List concrete router or operator decisions made from per-host token sums that cannot be made from limit/remaining/reset fields; if list is empty, redundancy holds

claims.claim: UI comments claiming tokens are architecturally always null are stale
claims.evidence: Brief F4: public/index.html:1081-1083, :703-705 vs tokens-hook.sh Stop-hook design landed in 02e326e/cd78c58

challenges.their_claim: Most of the machinery already exists, so the remaining gap may be worth closing
challenges.problem: Treats sunk server/UI plumbing as pressure to ship. The gap is not a small wire — it is an unvalidated producer with known semantic corruption (C1), an undocumented dependency (C2), and an unmeasured accuracy failure mode on the dominant workload (C5). Machinery without a correct producer is not 'almost done'; it is a UI lie waiting for a bad number.
challenges.test: Before any wire decision: pass E1 (U2) and write one sentence naming the user question the column answers that limit/reset does not

challenges.their_claim: Author argues tokens and tps stay correct because prompt rows carry tokens=null
challenges.problem: Even if tps arithmetic is correct, the dashboard displays requests too. Trading a working metric for a speculative one is not 'acceptable cost' — it is moving the empty-state honesty problem from tokens onto requests. Also tps = tokens/3600 is only as meaningful as the composite token definition (C4).
challenges.test: Mock two rows per turn (prompt null-tokens + stop with tokens) through /api/stats and show the exact requests and tps operators would see; decide if that requests figure is still fit for display

challenges.their_claim: A dashboard for a token-budget-aware account router arguably has token usage as its most natural headline metric
challenges.problem: aigate is not in the request path and does not meter budgets from this column today. The working budget signal is limits/resets. 'Arguably natural' is product poetry until someone shows the column changing an account-selection outcome.
challenges.test: Trace one real routing decision end-to-end; cite whether request_log.tokens is read. If not, headline-metric claim is false for current code.

needs_research: E1/U2: In Claude Code session JSONL, is assistant message usage per-message or cumulative across the turn?
U3: Does Claude Code expose token usage via a supported hook input field, OTel, or CLI JSON output without parsing transcript JSONL?
U4: What Stop-hook contract do aaa-selfimprove.sh and nohumans.js journal --hook already rely on (stdin payload shape)?
U5: What single operator question should the column answer — cost, context pressure, burn rate, or something else?
Does any server path read request_log.tokens for routing, or is it display-only?
dissent: I will not agree to wire tokens-hook.sh as-is under any consensus that hand-waves C1 or C5. Minimum bar: (1) E1 shows last-message usage is cumulative OR the hook sums all assistant usage blocks in the turn, (2) requests double-count is fixed (PATCH/update-by-session or stop counting empty-prompt rows) before enablement, (3) column header/semantics match a defined question — not a four-way undenominated sum. Until then the honest move is delete the UI column (keep schema + aggregator for cheap revival; quarantine the hook as un-installed proposal). Single cheapest experiment for the chair: pick one multi-tool-use session JSONL, extract every assistant message usage block in the last turn in order, print input/output/cache fields per message, and report whether each field is strictly per-message or monotonically cumulative — that kills or confirms C5 in one pass.
